title: Assignment file (rtm-assign-1.0)
description: One enumerator's households for one round, written by the team leader. It holds the names and phone numbers of that enumerator's households only. File name: {enumerator_id}_assignment_R{round, two digits}.json, for example E07_assignment_R05.json. Fields not listed here are kept but ignored by the tool.

program.description: The program's code, for example L2MN-DEMO.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Selects the bundled holiday table the calendar shows outside the round window.

generated_by.description: The leader who generated the file.

revision.description: 1 for the files written before the round; 2, 3… for revised files written after households were moved during the round.

supersedes.description: Revised file: the fingerprint of this enumerator's earlier file, which this one replaces.

matching.description: The leader's matching criteria for the round and this enumerator's values: a household goes only to an enumerator whose values for each criterion include the household's.

criteria.description: Columns of the household list, for example language, respondent_sex, region.

enumerator.description: This enumerator's values for each criterion.

rule.description: How the households were assigned. 'keep_same' is the handbook's stated default (Section 3.5.3): keep the same enumerator, rotate a planned share each round, switch the enumerator for a household that becomes hard to reach.

order_by.description: Equal split and share of total: the column the list is ordered by before it is cut into blocks (psu, stratum, language or hhid).

method.description: Share of total: households placed by blocks of the ordered list, or dealt at random.

synthetic.description: True for sample files: no real household, name or number.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the whole file without this field. The tool warns, and logs, when it does not match.

estimated.description: The source marks the date as estimated (for example a lunar holiday).

working.description: Set by the leader: the call center works that day.

dial_cap.description: The program's stopping rule, in dials per household per round.

day_list.description: The day list: how many households the enumerator's Today tab offers at most each day, the calls due first and then households pulled forward from later days, so that unanswered calls leave nobody waiting. The leader's number, or 1.5 × the planned first dials per day.

contact_protocol.description: The leader's contact protocol (3 November 2026): how the enumerator's list plans the next call after an unanswered one. Absent: two hours apart, no daily or day limit, the usual hour each day.

per_day.description: At most this many calls a day to one household; then the next working day.

gap_hours.description: At least this many hours between two calls to one household on the same day (2 by default).

days.description: A household never reached (no call with contact) is done after this many working days of calls, counted from its first call, as at the dial cap.

vary_times.description: Each new day of calls starts in the part of the day tried least so far for the household (morning until 12:00, afternoon until 17:00, evening), at its usual hour when that falls in the part.

self_scheduling.description: What the enumerator may change in their own schedule, set by the leader (3 November 2026). Absent: both allowed, first calls held to the latest first dial the file plans.

reschedule.description: May move a household's next call themselves, with a reason (event 'plan'). A respondent's callback is never moved this way.

availability.description: May mark a day or half day off (event 'availability'); the calls planned then move to their next working time.

push_first_calls.description: May move a household's first call past first_calls_by.

first_calls_by.description: The last day of the round's first-call period (the plan's spread over the window, Section 3.4).

last_status.description: The result of the last dial on this number last round.

hhid.description: Household ID, as text, so leading zeros survive.

tz.description: IANA time zone, only where the program spans several.

last3.description: Interviewed in each of the last three rounds, oldest first.

matched.description: Only when the round has matching criteria: whether this enumerator matches the household. False when the leader moved it by hand regardless.

replacements.description: This household's replacements, in the order they are used.

criteria.description: Only when the round has matching criteria: the household's value for each, for example language: kk.

handover.description: Only for a household moved to this enumerator during the round: what the previous enumerator did. Those dials count toward the dial cap.
